discovery: Invention and realization of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the 'magic wavelength' optical lattice, which traps many neutral atoms without perturbing the clock transition, and demonstrated the first lattice clocks. Ye turned the idea into the world's most precise and accurate clocks, reaching uncertainties at the 1e-18 level and below through careful control of density shifts, blackbody radiation and lattice light shifts, and pioneering many-body and spin-squeezing techniques. Together they improved timekeeping by about two orders of magnitude over caesium standards. These clocks resolve the gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences, enable relativistic geodesy (Katori's Tokyo Skytree test), set leading limits on variations of fundamental constants and ultralight dark matter, and are driving the redefinition of the SI second. This is a new measurement capability with a clear error budget, opening tests of fundamental physics on a laboratory bench.
